Triggers.value: Feeling physically restrained or held down

Threat.value: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns
My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed

issues.item: Triggers: Expressions of Affection: Physical affection such as hugs
issues.explanation: For captivity trauma, 'being followed or tracked' is a plausible trigger, but 'expressions of affection' and 'being praised' are a very different interpersonal trigger pattern and are weakly anchored to the rest of the profile. Taken together, the trigger set lacks a coherent captivity-related theme strongly linking to the selected threat and memory items.

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: Within Threat, repeated door/lock checking and frequent false alarms imply strong danger monitoring and protection seeking, whereas 'taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm' points in the opposite direction. These can coexist in some patients, but here they sit awkwardly with the rest of the profile and are not supported by other items.

issues.item: Memory: Story Feels Unreal: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
issues.explanation: The memory profile is mostly sensory/intrusive (taste vividness, visual memories), which fits strong Triggers→Memory and Memory→Threat links. 'Story feels unreal' instead suggests a more dissociative/derealized stance that is not well integrated with the rest of the memory and appraisal profile selected here.
